card.title: Calculation of Empirical and Molecular Formula from Percentage Composition

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **empirical formula** gives the simplest whole-number atom ratio; the **molecular formula** gives the true atom count and equals the empirical formula multiplied by n = molecular mass ÷ empirical mass. The four-step ritual — assume 100 g, convert to moles, divide by the smallest, clear fractions (0.5→×2, 0.33→×3, 0.25→×4) — turns percentage composition into the empirical formula: 40% C, 6.67% H, 53.33% O → CH₂O…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass - Molecular formula = (empirical formula)ₙ - % element = (atoms × atomic mass ÷ M) × 100 - Combustion: mol C = mol CO₂; mol H = 2 × mol H₂O

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Empirical mass vs molecular mass:** empirical mass = mass of the simplest unit (CH₂O = 30); molecular mass = mass of the true molecule (C₆H₁₂O₆ = 180). n = 180/30 = 6.  ·  **Ratio vs substance:** CH₂O is the empirical formula of glucose, formaldehyde AND acetic acid — the empirical formula alone cannot identify a compound.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Molecular formula = (empirical formula)ₙ where n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Fe 69.9%, O 30.1%*** — ratio 1 : 1.5 → ×2 → Fe₂O₃, haematite: the classic ore-analysis variant.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Reading a Formula Backwards Percentage composition is chemistry's fingerprint: measure what percentage of a compound's mass each element occupies, and the **empirical formula** (simplest whole-number atom ratio) follows by arithmetic. Multiply by n = M/empirical-mass and the **molecular formula** — the true atom count — appears. NEB has asked this three years running (2020, 2022, 2024).  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The two formulas | Formula | Definition | Example (glucose) | |---|---|---| | **Empirical** | Simplest whole-number ratio of atoms | CH₂O | | **Molecular** | Actual number of atoms per molecule | C₆H₁₂O₆ | Molecular formula = (empirical formula)ₙ, where **n = molecular mass ÷ empirical-formula mass**. ### 2.2 The four-step ritual (percentage → empirical formula) 1.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2022/2020 (3m): A compound contains 40% C, 6.67% H and 53.33% O by mass. Calculate its empirical formula.** — Per 100 g: C = 40/12 = 3.33 mol; H = 6.67/1 = 6.67 mol; O = 53.33/16 = 3.33 mol. Divide by 3.33 → C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1 → **CH₂O**.  ·  **NEB 2024 (2m): A compound has empirical formula CH₂O and molar mass 180 g/mol. Find its molecular formula.** — Empirical mass = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30; n = 180/30 = 6; molecular formula = **C₆H₁₂O₆** (glucose).

rows.text: Show all four steps — NEB awards a mark per step even if the final formula slips.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Four steps: 100 g → moles → divide by smallest → clear fractions. n = molecular mass ÷ empirical mass. 40/6.67/53.33 → CH₂O (2022, 2020); ×6 → C₆H₁₂O₆ (2024).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Empirical formulas were how chemists first pinned down composition — Avogadro's followers (Cannizzaro) used them to fix atomic masses.

rows.text: Limit to remember: 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ entities (avogadro constant, nₐ). molar mass (m) is g·mol⁻¹; for a compound m = σ(atomic masses).
